measures.title: Regional Transit Measure
measures.summary: Would enact a sales tax of 0.5% in Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties and 1% in San Francisco for 14 years, estimated to raise about $980 million a year. The money would go to transit service including BART, Caltrain, VTA, SamTrans, AC Transit and Muni, to transit safety, cleanliness, affordability and reliability, and to repairing targeted roads and potholes, with financial transparency and oversight requirements. It is decided by a majority of all votes cast across the five-county Public Transit Revenue Measure District.
measures.yesMeans: You want to enact the regional transit sales tax for 14 years.
measures.noMeans: You do not want to enact the tax.

measures.title: City of Oakland Charter Amendment Measure
measures.summary: Would amend the Oakland City Charter to make the Mayor, rather than the City Administrator, the City's chief executive over most departments, give the Mayor a veto (including a line-item budget veto) that six councilmembers could override, and end the Mayor's tie-breaking vote. It would let the Council confirm certain department heads, create an Independent Budget and Legislative Analyst, and hold hearings with subpoena power. It would require councilmembers to work full time and have the Public Ethics Commission set salaries for the Mayor and councilmembers.
measures.yesMeans: You want to amend the Charter to make the Mayor the chief executive and make the other listed changes.
measures.noMeans: You do not want to make these Charter changes.

measures.title: City of Oakland Real Property Tax Measure
measures.summary: Would amend Oakland's Real Property Transfer Tax so that transfers through foreclosure, or in lieu of foreclosure, are taxed, based on the property's fair market value. Exceptions would remain for transfers converting commercial property to certain housing or healthcare uses, transfers to community banking organizations, and certain transfers of residential properties of four units or less, and the Council could change these exceptions by ordinance. Revenue would go to the general fund for any city purpose.
measures.yesMeans: You want to apply Oakland's real property transfer tax to most foreclosure-related transfers.
measures.noMeans: You want foreclosure-related transfers to stay generally exempt from the tax.
